title: Entanglement and the Bell States
summary: Tensor products, the CNOT gate, Bell states and qubit ordering.
objectives: Prepare the Bell state |Φ⁺⟩ with a Hadamard and a CNOT gate
Choose the control and target qubits of a CNOT gate
Decide whether a two-qubit state is a product state by comparing a₀₀a₁₁ with a₀₁a₁₀
mission: Prepare the Bell state |Φ⁺⟩ = (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2 on qubits 0 and 1.
hints: Put qubit 0 in superposition with a Hadamard gate: qc.h(0). At this point each qubit still has a Bloch vector of length 1.
The CNOT flips the target when the control is 1. Use qubit 0 as control and qubit 1 as target: qc.cx(control, target).
Apply qc.h(0), then qc.cx(0, 1). With the cursor on the CNOT line, the Bloch vectors shrink to the center of the sphere.

prediction.question: The state (|00⟩ + |01⟩ − |10⟩ − |11⟩)/2 has four nonzero amplitudes. Is it entangled?
options: Yes: with all four amplitudes nonzero, the qubits are correlated
No: it is a product state, since a₀₀a₁₁ = a₀₁a₁₀
It cannot be decided without measuring both qubits
prediction.explanation: Here a₀₀a₁₁ = (1/2)(−1/2) = −1/4 and a₀₁a₁₀ = (1/2)(−1/2) = −1/4, so the product test is satisfied. The state is |−⟩ on qubit 1 and |+⟩ on qubit 0. Having several nonzero amplitudes does not imply entanglement.
